trial_court: Court of MS. JAYANTI CHANDER, Judicial Magistrate First Class (NI Act) - 07, South District, Saket Courts, New Delhi.
facts_of_case: Complainant Sh. Anuj Dhamija filed a complaint against accused Sh. Hira Singh for dishonour of cheque bearing number 216801 dated 06.06.2019 for an amount of Rs. 36,00,000/- drawn by Corporation Bank, Neb Sarai Branch, New Delhi.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the accused to prove that he did not receive the amount.
legal_principles.held: In response, the accused reiterated the defence taken in the notice framed under section 251, CrPC. The accused stated that he did not receive an amount of Rs. 18 lakhs from the complainant and did not enter into any agreement to sell with the complainant.

legal_principles.principle: The accused's statement under section 313, CrPC should be considered while evaluating the evidence.
legal_principles.held: STATEMENT UNDER SECTION 313 CRPC ... wherein the entire incriminating evidence was put to him. In response, the accused reiterated the defence taken in the notice framed under section 251, CrPC.

outcome.final_order: The court acquitted the accused Sh. Hira Singh.

use_for_drafting: drafting a complaint case for cheque bounce
defending an accused in a cheque bounce case
advising on the legal implications of dishonored cheques
